summary: Post-market read: total risk score 44.77 (caution), up 0.75 on the day, regime still goldilocks, but the energy and rate levers tightened together. Brent crude settled at 101.21 dollars (+3.36%), the first close above 100 since 2026-07-24, and the EIA lifted its 2026 Brent average forecast to 91 dollars; the 2-year Treasury yield rose to 4.37 (previous 4.34), and the FedWatch implied rate 3.955 sits above the current effective rate 3.63, so markets have re-priced a hike. Inside equities the tape was extremely split: memory gained 1.33% and networking 0.94%, while data_centers fell 2.65% and fintech 1.84%; MU rose 2.86% to 1028.85 and AMD 2.70% to 519.39, while NVDA slipped 0.78%. The A-share memory chain weakened, with 301308.SZ down 3.02% and 688825.SH down 2.60%. Crypto barely moved, with BTC at 78522. PPI tomorrow and CPI the day after will decide the Fed's rate call.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Energy-inflation repricing: Brent crude settled at 101.21 dollars, up 3.29 dollars (+3.36%), the first close above 100 since 2026-07-24; the EIA lifted its 2026 Brent average forecast to 91 dollars, and the crack spread between refined products and crude is becoming the global central banks' inflation warning gauge.

Rate repricing: the 2-year Treasury yield rose to 4.37 (previous 4.34), with the 10-year at 4.78; the FedWatch implied rate 3.955 sits above the current effective rate 3.63, so markets have re-priced a hike; the US 30-year mortgage rate climbed to 6.85%, the highest in more than a year.
The real-rate constraint is unresolved: the 10-year real rate at 2.43 sits at the 98.72 percentile, and the macro dimension score 61.54 remains the heaviest risk source.

AI leadership narrowed: memory gained 1.33%, networking 0.94% and semis 0.88% (MU up 2.86%, AMD up 2.70%), but data_centers fell 2.65%, fintech 1.84% and gaming 1.71%; NVDA slipped 0.78% and AVGO 1.28%, with semis_relative at -9.07.
Labor resilience holds but is fraying at the edge: payrolls added 162 (previous 21), unemployment steady at 4.1, weekly claims rose to 206000 (previous 204000), and participation ticked up to 61.6.

supporting_signals.claim: Volatility stays low: VIX at 15.72 (previous 15.3) and realized volatility 8.36 — low volatility continues to underpin the goldilocks regime.
Credit stays calm: the high-yield spread at 2.67 (previous 2.68) and the IG spread at 0.81 show no sign of credit stress.
Crypto is unperturbed: BTC at 78522, up 0.1% on the day — risk appetite has not been broken by the energy shock.

contradicting_signals.claim: Breadth is thin: only 60% of members sit above the 200-day average, the new-highs ratio 1.29% trails the new-lows ratio 4.52%, and the small-cap relative is -1.53.
The direction signals disagree: model confidence 0.9212 confirms full data coverage, yet the intraday rise in the total score 44.77 coexists with the macro dimension at 61.54.

what_changed_today: Brent crude settled at 101.21 dollars (+3.36%), the first close above 100 since 2026-07-24.
The 2-year Treasury yield rose to 4.37 (previous 4.34), and the FedWatch implied rate 3.955 sits above the effective rate 3.63.
MU rose 2.86% to 1028.85 and AMD 2.70% to 519.39, AI leadership narrowed to memory (+1.33%), while data_centers fell 2.65%.
Apple unveiled its first foldable iPhone Duo at 1999 dollars (15999 yuan in China), with preorders opening 2026-10-16.
The total risk score is 44.77, up 0.75 on the day; VIX rose to 15.72.
watch_next: PPI lands 2026-09-10 and CPI 2026-09-11 — the two inflation reports that will decide the Fed's hike call.
Whether Brent holds above 100 and whether the 2-year yield keeps climbing.

bull_case.title: Bull case: soft inflation prints unwind the hike pricing
points: If PPI and CPI come in below expectations, the 2-year yield retreats from 4.37 and the hike pricing unwinds.
Brent back below 100 eases energy-inflation pressure, with VIX already low at 15.72.

base_case.title: Base case: the total score holds in the 40 to 50 band as caution
points: The total score 44.77 oscillates in a low-volatility band and the goldilocks regime holds.
The Fed waits for the CPI on 2026-09-11 before deciding.

bear_case.title: Bear case: a hot CPI print tightens the real-rate constraint
points: If CPI surprises hot and Brent holds above 100, the real-rate constraint at 2.43 (the 98.72 percentile) tightens further.
The new-lows ratio 4.52% already exceeds the new-highs ratio; if breadth deteriorates the total score pushes toward 55.
